question: What is the primary objective of a health financing system?

options.A: To improve health outcomes and protect from financial hardship
options.B: To maximize profit for private pharmaceutical manufacturers
options.C: To increase out-of-pocket spending in rural clinics
options.D: To reduce the total number of operational public hospitals

explanation: Health financing aims to ensure people get needed care without facing poverty from medical bills. [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h1)

question: Risk pooling in health financing serves which main function?

options.A: Generating direct revenue for private medical laboratories
options.B: Sharing financial risk across a larger group of people
options.C: Eliminating the need for purchasing health commodities
options.D: Ensuring only wealthy individuals pay for health services

explanation: Pooling spreads the financial burden of illness from the sick individual to the broader population. [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h1)

question: Efficiency in health care financing is best defined as:

options.A: Collecting taxes without offering clinical services
options.B: Limiting patient admissions to reduce staff workload
options.C: Spending the highest possible budget on infrastructure
options.D: Maximizing health outcomes from available resources

explanation: Efficiency focuses on achieving the best possible results without wasting scarce resources. [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h2)

question: A primary health center uses fewer bandages and drugs to achieve the same healing rate. This demonstrates:

options.B: A reduction in the quality of nursing care
options.C: Failure to meet minimum clinical standards
options.D: Increased dependency on external donor funds

explanation: Using fewer inputs to achieve the same clinical output represents an increase in operational efficiency. [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h2)

question: Allocative efficiency is primarily concerned with:

options.A: Using fewer syringes during a single injection procedure
options.B: Reducing the salaries of administrative hospital staff
options.C: Increasing out-of-pocket payments at the pharmacy
options.D: Distributing resources across different health programs

explanation: Allocative efficiency involves choosing the right mix of health interventions to fund. [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h3)

question: A clinic nurse ensures no cotton wool or gloves are wasted during wound dressing procedures. This practice demonstrates:
explanation: Technical efficiency relates to minimizing waste and producing specific services at the lowest cost. [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h3)

question: Effectiveness in health care measures:

options.A: The total cost of purchasing medical equipment
options.B: Real-world health benefits produced by an intervention
options.C: The speed at which administrative reports are filed
options.D: How many patients visit a clinic each month

explanation: Effectiveness assesses if a treatment actually works when used in normal clinical practice. [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h4)

question: Why does real-world effectiveness sometimes differ from clinical trial efficacy?

options.A: Everyday clinical settings involve varied patient adherence and resource limits
options.B: Patients in hospitals never follow prescription instructions
options.C: Doctors in rural clinics lack basic medical training
options.D: Clinical trials always overestimate the cost of medications

explanation: Real-world conditions introduce variables like inconsistent drug supply and patient compliance that clinical trials control for. [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h4)

question: Equity in health care financing means that contributions should be based on:
explanation: Fair financing requires those with higher income to contribute more, protecting the poor from financial ruin. [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h5)

question: Which payment method creates the greatest barrier to equity in low-income settings?
explanation: Direct out-of-pocket payments disproportionately burden poor households, limiting their access to necessary care. [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h5)

question: Horizontal equity requires that individuals with equal health needs receive:
explanation: Horizontal equity ensures equal treatment for people with equal medical needs. [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h6)

question: Charging higher health insurance premiums to high-income earners than to low-income earners is an example of:
explanation: Vertical equity involves treating people with different abilities to pay differently to achieve fairness. [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h6)

question: Why can pursuing pure technical efficiency sometimes conflict with equity?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any government health budget
options.B: It forces urban hospitals to treat emergency cases without payment
options.C: It always results in higher out-of-pocket payments for wealthy individuals
options.D: It may lead to closing low-volume rural clinics that vulnerable populations depend on

explanation: Focusing only on cost-per-patient can penalize remote areas where serving fewer people is more expensive but equitable. [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h7)

question: A health reform policy that expands primary care coverage for rural poor while controlling costs demonstrates:

options.B: A balance of efficiency, effectiveness, and equity
options.D: A violation of horizontal equity principles

explanation: Successful health systems strive to harmonize cost-effective care with fair access for all segments of the population. [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h7)
